svg.title: Preview environment replicas across clusters
svg.desc: On a laptop, the developer runs mirrord preview start, stop, or status with the mirrord CLI against the mirrord operator on the Primary cluster, which is management-only. The Primary operator sends one copy of the preview to every workload cluster. On the Default cluster, the operator runs the original preview task. The preview pods steal matched HTTP traffic that enters that cluster and reach the branch DB pod by pod IP, with no tunnel. On the member cluster, the operator runs the replica copy, and replica pods steal matched HTTP traffic that enters that cluster. The customer load balancer sends live traffic into any cluster. A replica reaches the branch DB in four steps. One: the app container connects to the db sidecar at 127.0.0.1 on the branch port. Two: the sidecar connects to the local operator's tunnel gateway over mTLS. Three: the request travels on one HTTP/2 stream of the connection that the Primary dials in through the member cluster's API server. Four: the Primary authorizes the request, then port-forwards to the branch DB pod through the Default cluster's API server. The member namespace holds no cluster credential. On both clusters, the deployed app's patched consumer sends matched messages into one shared temp queue, and the previews compete-consume it, so each message is handled once.
svg.text: sends one copy of the preview to every workload cluster
created once by the Default cluster's split; each message is handled once
How a replica reaches the branch DB
The app connects to the sidecar at 127.0.0.1:<branch port>.
The sidecar connects to the local operator's gateway over mTLS. The hello names the branch, and the cert uid is the identity.
The request uses one HTTP/2 stream on the connection that the Primary dials in through the member API server.
The Primary authorizes it, then port-forwards to the branch DB pod through the Default API server. No cluster credential is in the member namespace.
